body.heading: About this poster
paragraphs: Free SparkKindly Kids how things work printable poster: How Photosynthesis Works.

This poster explains photosynthesis step by step: a leaf catches sunlight, the roots drink water, tiny openings take in air, and the plant turns them into its own food — releasing the oxygen we breathe as it goes. Big labels and one idea per box, made for reading together before a walk to spot it happening.

body.heading: How to use this sheet
paragraphs: Print it big if you can and read it together, pointing to each label as you name it. Then cover the words and see how much you can explain from the pictures alone — that explaining-back is where the learning sticks.

body.heading: Talk about it
paragraphs: What three things does a plant need to make its food?
What gas do plants give back to the air?
Why do most leaves turn toward the light?

takeaway: Plants cook their own food from sunlight, water and air — and the leftovers they release are the oxygen we breathe.
materials: A printer and one sheet of paper (letter or A4) — or just a screen to view it on
supervision: Read together the first time: an adult reads the labels aloud and answers the questions the poster raises.
safetyNotes: A reading poster — no tools, parts or experiments. If you try the real thing afterwards (a magnet hunt, a proper handwash), a grown-up leads.
Print at 100% size (not "fit to page") so the poster keeps its true proportions.
screenFreeExtension: Explain it back: after reading, put the poster away and tell a grown-up how it works in your own words — then draw your own version.
